# melbheat

**melbheat** helps a council or emergency-planning officer answer one
question: *have days above a chosen temperature become more frequent at
Melbourne Airport since 1970, and does the answer depend on what counts
as “hot”?*

**Documentation site:
<https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/>**
(function reference and a vignette that walks through the analysis and
the app).

## Quick start

``` r

library(melbheat)
ex <- annual_exceedances(threshold = 35)   # days a year above 35 °C
plot_exceedances(ex, split_year = 2000)    # chart: 8.2 vs 11.8 days a year
```

Each year is only counted if at least 80% of its days were recorded, so
a partly missing year such as 2022 is shown in grey and left out of the
averages.

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss")
```

or

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss")
```

## Launch the app

``` r

library(melbheat)
run_app()
```

The app opens in your browser. Choose whether to count hot days or hot
nights, set the temperature threshold, pick the months and a comparison
year, then read the summary, the chart and the table. The **Does the
threshold matter?** tab checks the answer across many thresholds, and
the **Guide** tab explains each control, each field and how to read the
results. The app uses the `bslib` package; if it is missing,
[`run_app()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/run_app.md)
tells you how to install it.

## What is in the package

| Function | What it does |
|:---|:---|
| `melb_temp` | Daily maximum and minimum temperature at Melbourne Airport |
| [`annual_exceedances()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/annual_exceedances.md) | Days per year above a threshold, flagging years with too many missing days |
| [`summarise_periods()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/summarise_periods.md) | Average annual count before and after a chosen year |
| [`describe_periods()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/describe_periods.md) | Plain-language summary: what changed and how sure we are |
| [`threshold_sensitivity()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/threshold_sensitivity.md) | The same comparison repeated across many thresholds |
| [`plot_exceedances()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/plot_exceedances.md), [`plot_sensitivity()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/plot_sensitivity.md) | ggplot2 charts that state the finding in the title |
| [`run_app()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/run_app.md) | Launches the Shiny app |

## Data

`melb_temp` holds one row per calendar day from 1 January 1970 to 26
July 2022 for the Melbourne Airport weather station (Bureau of
Meteorology station 086282): date, year, month, daily maximum (`tmax`)
and minimum (`tmin`) temperature in degrees Celsius, and the Bureau’s
quality flag for each. Days without an observation are kept as `NA`.
Readings that accumulate over more than one day are set to `NA`.

Source: Australian Bureau of Meteorology, Climate Data Online,
<http://www.bom.gov.au/climate/data/> (products IDCJAC0010 and
IDCJAC0011). Copyright Commonwealth of Australia, Bureau of Meteorology;
used here for educational purposes with attribution. The raw files and
the script that prepares them (`data-raw/melb_temp.R`) are in the
repository, so the data set can be rebuilt from scratch. The MIT licence
covers the package code, not the data.

## Limits

This is one weather station, readings are as recorded (not adjusted for
instrument or site changes), and the comparison shows *that* hot days
were more frequent later, not *why*.

# Package index

## Launch the app

One call opens the Shiny app in your browser.

- [`run_app()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/run_app.md)
  : Launch the Melbourne Airport heat explorer

## Count and compare

The analysis behind the app. Each function takes the output of the one
before it.

- [`annual_exceedances()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/annual_exceedances.md)
  : Count the days each year above a temperature threshold
- [`summarise_periods()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/summarise_periods.md)
  : Compare the average annual count before and after a year
- [`describe_periods()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/describe_periods.md)
  : Say what a period comparison shows, and how sure we can be
- [`threshold_sensitivity()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/threshold_sensitivity.md)
  : Does the conclusion depend on what counts as "hot"?

## Draw the results

ggplot2 charts that state the finding in their title.

- [`plot_exceedances()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/plot_exceedances.md)
  : Chart the number of hot days (or nights) per year
- [`plot_sensitivity()`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/plot_sensitivity.md)
  : Chart whether the conclusion depends on the threshold

## Data

Daily temperatures at Melbourne Airport, 1970 to 2022.

- [`melb_temp`](https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/reference/melb_temp.md)
  : Daily temperatures at Melbourne Airport, 1970 to 2022
